d877e29 zsh: add ~/.local/share/zsh/site-functions to fpath

content.text:
Done — added, applied, committed, pushed.

**Change** (`zsh.nix:128`, right before `compinit`):
```
fpath=("$HOME/.local/share/zsh/site-functions" $fpath)
```
Prepended, so it wins over the profile/plugin dirs.

**Why it's not default:** zsh has zero XDG awareness — it predates the basedir spec and still only special-cases `~/.zshrc` / `$ZDOTDIR`. The default `fpath` is baked in at compile time and points only at the install prefix (here `/nix/store/…-zsh-5.9.2/share/zsh/5.9.2/functions`). Everything else in your `fpath` is added by something: home-manager appends `$profile/share/zsh/site-functions`, the plugin block appends plugin dirs, and you append `~/.config/zsh/.zfunc`. There's no per-user "site-functions" convention at all, so no one ships a default for it.

Try it: `exec zsh` then `print -l $fpath | head -3`.
